problem:
The mass $M(t),$ in micrograms, of a sample of neon-19 is given by

$$
M(t)=4.5{e}^{-kt},
$$

where $t$ is the time, in seconds. The half-life of neon-19 is $17.2\,\text{s}.$ Rounded to **three significant figures**, what is the value of $k?$

$k≈$
{{field-1}} ${\text{s}}^{-1}$
worked_solution:
The mass $M(t)$ of a radioactive substance at time $t$ can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
{M}^{′}(t)=-kM(t),\,M(0)={M}_{0}.
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
M(t)={M}_{0}{e}^{-kt}.
$$

The half-life ${t}_{1/2}$ is the time taken for the mass of the substance to reduce by one half and is given by

$$
{t}_{1/2}=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{k}.
$$

Since we know that ${t}_{1/2}=17.2\,\text{s},$ we have

$$
17.2=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{k}\,⇒\,k=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{17.2}≈0.0403\,{\text{s}}^{-1}.
$$
